content: How does one check in CI that all the theorem in one's project only uses the three trusted axioms? How does mathlib do this? I have tried set_option linter.all true and that doesn't seem to flag uses of axiom. I do see that in daily.yml, mathlib is checked with nanoda, which appears to have a list of permitted axioms in the config. Is there more?
I actually do not think that there is any automated verification that axioms are not introduced, other than being careful in code review...
Although the external checkers would probably pick up on this, once they run.

Damiano Testa said:

I actually do not think that there is any automated verification that axioms are not introduced, other than being careful in code review...

As mentioned by Shreyas, there is a CI script that checks Mathlib with Nanoda every day. This would flag any axioms beyond the standard axioms (and Lean.trustCompiler, which is there for a technical reason).
And once Lean.trustCompiler is fully deprecated, it will be possible to check with Nanoda that only the standard axioms are being used.

I wish there was a standard way to do this. I noticed that lean4checker has become part of the toolchain as leanchecker. I also searched on Zulip after writing this message, and found Damiano’s script for Classical.choice but it ground vscode to a halt. That is why it makes sense to me to push this to CI rather than run it locally.
i'm also interested in seeing if there is a workflow to make it easier for reviewers to review lean compiled proofs to ensure that they are valid

Shreyas Srinivas said:

I noticed that lean4checker has become part of the toolchain as leanchecker.

Do you know if there's any documentation of this? I can't get it to work and leanchecker --help doesn't do anything.
Sorry that's the trust page. This one here :https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Build-Tools-and-Distribution/#build-tools-and-distribution
I was hoping for more detailed documentation than that.
I think you just run lake env leanchecker —fresh
